question:
An investigator is studying physiologic renal responses to common medical conditions. She measures urine osmolalities in different parts of the nephron of a human subject in the emergency department. The following values are obtained:
Portion of nephron Osmolality (mOsmol/kg)
Proximal convoluted tubule 300
Loop of Henle, descending limb 1200
Loop of Henle, ascending limb 250
Distal convoluted tubule 100
Collecting duct 1200
These values were most likely obtained from an individual with which of the following condition?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Loop of Henle, descending limb osmolality 1200" -> "Loop of Henle, ascending limb osmolality 250" -> "Collecting duct osmolality 1200" -> "Dehydration" -> 95% CHAIN: "Proximal convoluted tubule osmolality 300" -> "Distal convoluted tubule osmolality 100" -> "Concentration gradient in the nephron" -> "Dehydration" -> 90% CHAIN: "Loop of Henle, descending limb osmolality 1200" -> "Loop of Henle, ascending limb osmolality 250" -> "Collecting duct osmolality 1200" -> "Furosemide overdose" -> 95%
analysis: The individual most likely has a condition that leads to concentrated urine, as indicated by the high urine osmolalities in the Loop of Henle (ascending limb) and Collecting duct. Among the given options, dehydration is the most likely condition that would result in such concentrated urine.
